analysis:
The supplied units cover docs/architecture/inference.md only. The base excerpt (lines 2366-2597) is Flint and Bonsai documentation. The head excerpt (lines 1-415) is the Nemotron Super and managed-slot documentation. The change is documentation-only: no code, wire contract, key handling or cache storage logic is modified in this batch. Per the patch hunks, the edits do three things. (1) They state that GLM variable-frame-rate video is now indexed by nominalFrameRate rather than refused with a 400. (2) They remove the sentence saying variable-frame-rate video is a deterministic 400. (3) They add an inline video label list (MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders) around head lines 1896-1899, which is truncated in the patch excerpt.

Security-relevant observations for the integration pass:
- The GLM VFR change implies a behavioral code change in the provider media path: the processor accepts VFR video. This touches the T-050/TB-003/TB-007 surface (media decode, memory admission). The doc still cites the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (GLM5NextProcessor.maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token cap and the media reservation (GLM5NextVisionBudget). Those bounds are unchanged, so no regression is evident from the docs alone. The accompanying source change is not in this batch, so it cannot be verified that frame-count and decode bounds hold for VFR tracks. For example, indexing by nominalFrameRate could mis-time frames, but that is a correctness issue rather than a security one.
- The head excerpt is cut off before the inline video label hunk and the rest of the head file, so that hunk is only partially visible. The label is described as only gating the path; the remainder is truncated and not verifiable.
- No prefix cache (T-041) text changes are visible. The media-excluded-from-prefix-lookup statement (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint) is retained, so cross-tenant reuse for media is unchanged.
- The Nemotron docs describe cache scope, bank sizing and admission without altering the stated T-041 scoping. Media requests without a scope stay cold, and with a scope they are bound to an identity.

No findings. Recommend that the integration pass check the corresponding GLM5NextProcessor/MediaIngest code changes for decode-bound enforcement on VFR video.
